160373.title: Spreadsheet: Vector column auto fit width issue when component values differ greatly
160373.feasibility_reason: The issue involves UI layout and column width calculation logic for vector types in the spreadsheet editor. While well-defined, it requires navigating Blender's custom UI and spreadsheet codebase without prior insider knowledge.
160373.problem_summary: Auto-fitting vector column widths in the Spreadsheet editor results in text truncation when vector component values have significantly differing lengths (e.g., [1000000000, 0, 0]), because width estimation measures the concatenated string or sum of lengths rather than scaling based on the widest component.
160373.root_cause_hypothesis: The vector column width calculation in `estimate_max_column_width` formats all components together and measures the aggregate width (or estimates length from the joined string). However, the spreadsheet draws vector components in equally-sized sub-columns. When one component is much longer than the others, its sub-column width (total column width divided by component count) is insufficient, causing truncation.
160373.suggested_approach: Adjust the column width estimation logic for multi-component types (vector, color, quaternion, etc.) so that the estimated width is calculated based on the maximum component width multiplied by the number of components (plus inter-component spacing/padding), ensuring that each sub-column is wide enough to display the longest value without truncation.
prerequisites: Working Blender build environment (C/C++ and CMake)
Familiarity with the Spreadsheet Editor (`space_spreadsheet`) and Blender's UI text measurement functions (e.g., `BLF_width` or `UI_fontstyle_string_width`)
implementation_steps: Locate the column width estimation logic in `source/blender/editors/space_spreadsheet/` (specifically `estimate_max_column_width` or equivalent function handling column auto-sizing).
Inspect how multi-component data types (Float2/3/4, Int2/3, Color, Quaternion) are formatted and measured during column width estimation versus how cells are partitioned during rendering.

Update the estimation logic for multi-component values so that instead of measuring the concatenated formatted string, it measures or estimates the text width of each component individually, determines the maximum component width, and calculates the total width as `max_component_width * num_components` plus the padding/separator gaps.
Ensure non-monospaced font width differences and UI margins/icons are properly taken into account so sub-cells do not truncate.
Verify that single-component columns (floats, ints, strings, booleans) remain unaffected by the change.

Test by opening the reproduction .blend file with vector values like `(1000000000, 0, 0)` and double-clicking the column divider to auto-fit width, checking that the widest component is fully visible and no truncation occurs.

153791.title: Sculpt: Add ability to toggle X, Y, Z radial symmetry independent of count
153791.feasibility_reason: The issue provides a clear task list for adding a toggle for radial symmetry independent of the count, but it touches multiple subsystems (UI, Paint struct data, and sculpting/painting logic) in a complex C/C++ codebase like Blender.
153791.problem_summary: Radial symmetry in Sculpt mode currently relies solely on a count per axis (where 1 means disabled), preventing users from toggling radial symmetry on/off independently of their chosen segment count or assigning hotkeys to toggle it.
153791.root_cause_hypothesis: The radial symmetry state is stored exclusively as segment counts in DNA (`Paint.radial_sym[3]`), conflating the enabled state with the segment count value. Consequently, disabling symmetry resets or overwrites the count, and no discrete boolean toggle exists in RNA or UI.
153791.suggested_approach: Introduce a bitmask flag in DNA (such as in `Paint` symmetry flags) for enabling radial symmetry on X, Y, and Z axes. Expose these toggles via RNA, update the sculpt/paint UI to show checkboxes alongside the count spinners, update sculpt execution code to check both the toggle flag and segment count, and add necessary do_versions logic.
prerequisites: A working Blender build environment from source (C/C++ and Python)
Understanding of Blender's DNA/RNA architecture and versioning system
Familiarity with sculpt and paint symmetry handling in Blender
implementation_steps: Define new flag bits in `DNA_brush_types.h` (e.g., `PAINT_RADIAL_SYM_X`, `PAINT_RADIAL_SYM_Y`, `PAINT_RADIAL_SYM_Z`) in `ePaintSymmetryFlags` or a new radial symmetry bitfield in the `Paint` struct.

Expose RNA boolean properties (e.g., `use_radial_symmetry_x`, `use_radial_symmetry_y`, `use_radial_symmetry_z` or a composite enum/flag `use_radial_symmetry`) on `Paint` / `Sculpt` in `source/blender/makesrna/intern/rna_sculpt_paint.c`.

Add versioning code in `source/blender/blenloader/intern/versioning_*.cc` to initialize the radial symmetry flags to true for axes where existing files have `radial_sym[i] > 1` (or maintain backward compatibility).

Update sculpt and paint symmetry iteration logic (e.g., in `sculpt.cc` / `sculpt_intern.hh` where radial symmetry passes are looped) to verify the axis flag is active before iterating beyond 1 repetition.

Update the Sculpt UI in Python (`properties_paint_common.py` or the symmetry popover in 3D Viewport header) to display toggle checkboxes for X, Y, Z next to their respective segment count inputs, disabling or muting the count input when the toggle is off.
Test sculpting with radial symmetry enabled, toggled off, and toggled back on, verifying that the configured segment count is preserved and keybindings can be assigned to the new RNA properties.

164257.title: Console: Mouse text selection does not continue through scrollback while dragging
164257.feasibility_reason: The issue describes a missing UI interaction feature (auto-scrolling during text selection drag) in Blender's Python Console. While the reproduction steps are clear, implementing continuous selection-dragging with auto-scroll requires deep knowledge of Blender's window manager event loop, UI drawing, and text editor/console event handling, making it moderately complex for an outsider.
blockers: Familiarity with Blender's custom UI event handling and console scrollback mechanism is needed.
164257.problem_summary: In the Blender Python Console editor, dragging the mouse to select text does not auto-scroll the console viewport when the cursor reaches the viewport boundaries, nor does Shift+Click properly extend an active selection across scrollback history.
164257.root_cause_hypothesis: The console mouse selection operator (`CONSOLE_OT_select_set` or modal click-drag operator in `source/blender/editors/space_console/console_ops.c`) does not support auto-scrolling when mouse coordinates fall outside the region bounds during drag modal execution, and it calculates selection coordinates relative to visible region lines without adjusting for scroll offset changes or supporting continuous Shift-click range extensions.
164257.suggested_approach: Implement auto-scrolling during the mouse drag modal state in the Console editor (similar to text editor / standard UI widgets) using a modal timer or view bounds check, and update the selection endpoint relative to the scrolled content buffer rather than clamped static screen space. Additionally, support Shift-click to extend the selection endpoint while preserving the original anchor.
prerequisites: Ability to build Blender from source (C/C++ environment)
Familiarity with Blender's Window Manager (WM) modal operator event loop, timer callbacks, and editor region navigation
implementation_steps: Locate the mouse selection operator and event handling for `SPACE_CONSOLE` in `source/blender/editors/space_console/console_ops.c`.
Examine how text selection coordinates are mapped from screen space (region mouse Y/X) to console line buffers and character offsets in `console_draw.c` and `console_ops.c`.
Add logic in the modal event loop of the selection operator to detect when the mouse pointer is dragged near or beyond the top or bottom edges of the console region.

Register a timer (`WM_event_add_modal_handler` / `WM_event_add_timer`) when dragging out of bounds to trigger incremental scrolling of `SpaceConsole->scroll` and dynamically refresh the selection end position.

Ensure `Shift + LEFTMOUSE` click behavior inspects existing selection state to update only the active selection endpoint (`sel_end`) while retaining the selection start (`sel_start`), rather than resetting both.

Verify edge cases: dragging past the top/bottom boundary stops scrolling when reaching the beginning or end of the history buffer, releasing the mouse cleans up modal timers, and text copying (`ctrl+c`) retains the entire multi-screen selection.
Test on multiple operating systems (macOS, Linux, Windows) with long multi-page text blocks.

136889.title: Scale Cage in ortho view scales other axis unintuitively
136889.feasibility_reason: The issue describes an unintuitive scaling behavior specific to the cage scale tool in orthographic views. While steps to reproduce are clear, figuring out the orthographic projection math vs. screen-space interaction for gizmos can be subtle without prior familiarity with the gizmo/transform system.
136889.problem_summary: When using the Scale Cage tool in an aligned orthographic view, dragging what visually appears to be a side handle unexpectedly scales the object along two axes instead of just the active view axis.
136889.root_cause_hypothesis: The 3D cage gizmo distinguishes between corner handles (3 axes), edge handles (2 axes), and face handles (1 axis). In an aligned orthographic view (e.g., Front view), the silhouette handles on the sides correspond to the cage's 3D edges (which scale along both the screen axis and depth axis), while the 1-axis face center handle is positioned directly in the center facing the camera or obscured. Users clicking the side handle expect a 1D scale along the visible screen axis.
136889.suggested_approach: Detect when the 3D cage gizmo is used in an aligned orthographic view (or when an edge handle is parallel to the view direction), and either project/constrain edge handle transformations to only affect the orthogonal screen axis (ignoring the depth axis), or adapt the gizmo handle hit-testing/display in orthographic projection so that side interactions behave as 1D face handles.
prerequisites: Ability to build Blender from source
Basic familiarity with Blender's gizmo architecture and orthographic view transform matrix math
implementation_steps: Locate the 3D cage gizmo implementation (typically under `source/blender/editors/gizmo_library/gizmo_types/cage3d_gizmo.cc` or `transform_gizmo_cage.cc`).
Analyze how cage handles are represented, selected, and mapped to scale transform axes during drag operations (distinguishing face, edge, and corner interactions).

Inspect the transform handler when dragging edge handles; determine how the view projection matrix or camera orientation can be queried (e.g., checking if the view is orthographic and aligned with a principal axis).

Implement logic in the cage drag operator / gizmo interaction callback to suppress or lock the depth axis when dragging an edge handle that lies parallel to the view direction in orthographic projection.
Verify whether gizmo drawing/highlighting in orthographic view needs adjustments to avoid visual confusion over which axis is being influenced.

Test behavior in Perspective view (verify standard 3-axis/2-axis/1-axis cage scaling is preserved) and in Top, Front, Right orthographic views (verify side handles only scale the expected screen axis).
